I’ve ordered from this place twice on Zomato since we are from Hyderabad and wanted to try their biryani. Both times, I ordered the Hyderabadi Chicken Dum Biryani and the Lucknow Biryani.

Unfortunately, they didn’t follow the cooking instructions on either occasion, even though I mentioned that the order was specially prepared for us. I had clearly asked for it to be spicy 🌶️, but it wasn’t. I also requested cutlery both times—they missed it the first time, and again the second time. Since I’m staying in a hotel where they don’t provide Cutlery or serve food, it became very inconvenient to serve directly from the containers.

I also ordered Phirni. The first time, it tasted really good, so I ordered two portions the second time—but the taste was so bad that I had to throw them away.

Even the Salan (gravy) was inconsistent. The first time, it was tasty though a bit watery. This time I ordered two portions (one large and one small), and both were a disaster — very thin and lacking flavor.

Verdict : For price they are charging quantity they are providing is not worth any way. They are paying extra for pots and billing same to us with profit on everything they used.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Amidst all the chaos going around, this brand never fails to surprise me and my family! ☺️

Ordered lunch today from here… for me and my mom.

We ordered for Veg Biryani and Paneer 65.

Paneer 65 was so so delicious and so nicely cooked and perfectly served in a disposable and safe box. Also, paneer was so soft making it even more delicious!

featured_reviews.name: Jatin Shah
featured_reviews.review_text:
In these times of pandemic, we finally ordered for food and this time around we were keen to have Biryani. Had heard of Biryani By Kilo and we decided to give it a try. Packaging was superb, leak proof. Food came in quite warm. Talking about what all we ordered -

Kebab Platter which comes with 4 kebabs - Veg Galouti, Crispy Corn Stick, Kaju Ki Seekh and Paneer Multani. The packaging was quite neat. Of this Crispy Corn Stick was absolutely brilliant, must try. Also loved the Veg Galouti, wasn't dry at all. In fact quite quite soft and fresh, melts in mouth. Same was the case with Kaju Ki Seekh.

We had also called for Hyderabadi Dum Biryani, comes in 1/2 kg or 1 kg packs. It's packed in Handis. You also get another small handi with tealight candles which help keeping the biryani warm. This is quite unique, haven't seen this concept in any other delivery kitchens. Biryani is yum, I most definitely recommend it. Looking forward to trying Paneer Biryani next time.

We also called for Matka Phirni for dessert. Comes in a cute small Handi again. Phirni is brilliant, not too sweet just perfect. Quite thick as well. Superb food from Biryani By Kilo, wishing all the best!

featured_reviews.name: Vivek Vetal
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Persian Darbar in Byculla after hearing a lot of buzz around it. Given its reputation and the constant crowd outside, my expectations were naturally quite high. However, my overall experience was somewhat mixed.

To start with the positives — the ambience is genuinely good. The interiors are well done, with a spacious seating layout and a proper family-restaurant vibe. It feels grand and lively, which explains the heavy footfall. Do note that the place is almost always crowded. If you’re planning to visit, I would strongly recommend booking a table in advance or reaching a little early to avoid the long waiting time.

Coming to the food — I tried the Moroccan Kebab, Murgh Lebnani, Murgh Zafrani Tikka, Bihari Boti, and Chicken Biryani. Honestly, I found most of the dishes average. The taste and quality were mediocre, nothing extraordinary— the kind of flavour you can easily find at many other restaurants on the same street. Given the hype around the place, I expected something more distinctive or memorable. The Moroccan Kebab and Murgh variants were okay, but they didn’t stand out in terms of spice balance or uniqueness. The Bihari Boti was a bit undercooked.

The Chicken Biryani was comparatively better than the rest — flavorful, well-cooked rice, and properly spiced. It was the highlight of the meal for me.

Service, however, was quite slow — probably because of the constant rush. Staff were polite, but you’ll need some patience.

Overall, I felt the place is slightly overhyped. If you’re a hardcore foodie looking for exceptional flavours, you can skip it. If you do visit, go with limited expectations about the taste and focus more on the ambience and overall experience rather than culinary excellence.

Office lunch plans? Listen up, corporate warriors! The Biryani Affair is your new best friend. They offer special corporate discounts for bulk orders, making it super easy and delicious to feed the whole team.

What really seals the deal for me? Quick delivery, genuinely authentic taste, and prices that won't break the bank. It's the trifecta of a perfect meal!

So, next time those hunger pangs hit, don't even think twice. Hit up Zomato or Swiggy and let The Biryani Affair take care of you. Trust me, your taste buds will thank you! 📞 Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re a true food lover, Noor Mohammadi Hotel is nothing short of heaven. I finally got to try their legendary Nalli Nihari, and honestly… it lives up to every bit of the hype.

The nihari was rich, slow-cooked to perfection, with the marrow melting into the gravy, bursting with deep, soulful flavors. Every spoon felt warm, comforting, and indulgent — the kind of dish that makes you pause and appreciate good food.

And just when I thought it couldn’t get better, the meal ended with their Rabdi. Thick, creamy, and perfectly balanced in sweetness, it was the ideal dessert to round off such a hearty feast. You can actually taste the patience and tradition in every bite.
No fancy plating, no unnecessary drama — just authentic, old-school flavors that hit straight to the heart. Noor Mohammadi doesn’t just serve food; it serves heritage on a plate.

featured_reviews.name: Shaikh Kadir
featured_reviews.review_text:
This place truly gave me a heartwarming experience and the kind of food that reminds you what real, honest cooking tastes like. It’s amazing to know that this restaurant has been around for over 102 years, carrying forward a legacy of authentic flavors and consistent quality. You can really feel that heritage in every dish they serve.

The food was absolutely delicious and clearly made with care and good-quality ingredients. I loved how every bite had that traditional touch — nothing fancy, just pure, flavorful food made right. My personal favorites were the Mutton Sanju Baba and the Haleem. The mutton was soft, juicy, and full of flavor, while the haleem was rich, creamy, and perfectly spiced — the kind that instantly makes you smile after the first spoonful.

The ambiance adds to the experience — simple, calm, and full of character. It feels like a place where stories have been shared for generations. The staff was really friendly and attentive, making sure we were comfortable and enjoying our food.

Overall, I’d say this isn’t just a restaurant it’s a part of culinary history. If you love traditional, soulful food that warms both your heart and your stomach, this place is a must-visit.

featured_reviews.name: Moumita Roy
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Noor Mohammadi Hotel and it was a truly memorable experience for anyone who loves authentic Mughlai food. This place is quite iconic and well-known for its rich, flavorful dishes.

The highlight, of course, is their legendary chicken dishes—especially the Chicken Sanju Baba, which is packed with bold spices and has a rich, indulgent taste. The food overall is delicious, with generous portions and that proper old-school Mumbai Mughlai flavor.

The ambience is simple and no-frills, but that’s part of its charm. It’s more about the food than the setting. The place is usually quite crowded, and you might have to wait a bit for a table, especially during peak hours.

Service is quick considering the rush, though it can feel a bit hectic at times. Hygiene and seating are decent but not luxurious, so it’s best to go in with the right expectations.

Overall, Noor Mohammadi is a must-visit if you’re looking to enjoy authentic, hearty Mughlai cuisine in Mumbai. It’s not about fine dining, but about great taste and a truly local food experience.

If you are looking for the absolute best Value-for-Money (VFM) BBQ experience in Mumbai right now, look no further than Utsav Barbeque in Lower Parel. They truly live up to the name—every meal feels like a celebration!

The main attraction is their unbelievable Early Bird Offer at just ₹649 for a completely Unlimited BBQ spread featuring over 25 items, including fantastic seafood and chicken options. For a LIVE BBQ experience in the heart of the city, this price is unmatched.

Seafood is the Star!
While they offer excellent chicken and other starters, the Seafood selection is the real winner. The Crab Lollipops were phenomenal—perfectly seasoned and grilled, with a satisfying smoky flavor. Similarly, the Prawns Koliwada were fresh, juicy, and packed with authentic spice. They are grilled live right at your table, ensuring everything is piping hot and tender. The Chicken Masala Lollipop was another highlight, proving they handle their poultry just as well as their seafood.

The restaurant has a lively, celebratory atmosphere. It’s definitely a Family & Kids Friendly space, making it perfect for those big family dinners or fun get-togethers with friends. For those planning a bigger event, they even have a dedicated Private Party Section that can host around 30 guests—ideal for birthdays or anniversaries!

Utsav Barbeque delivers an amazing experience without forcing you to empty your wallet. You get great quality seafood, an engaging live grill, and a massive unlimited spread, all at an incredibly affordable price point. Highly, highly recommended for a fantastic and affordable feast!

featured_reviews.review_text:

Salli Boti Bun Muska: this is a Parsi dish which I liked quite a lot. Very succulent salli boti stuffing inside the classic bun muska.

Murg Gilafi Seekh: I love seekh kebabs, though I didn't quite like this one due to overload of ginger.

Khade Masale ka Murg: a rich, medium spicy chicken gravy dish which I loved. Went well with butter rotis. Chicken chunks were quite tender and juicy.

Hyderabadi Mutton Dum Biryani: This was the best dish out of all. Loved the aromatic biryani with soft and delicious mutton pieces. Well balanced on spice.

Jalebi Rabri: Perfect end to a hearty meal with crispy jalebi and creamy rabri.

They had also provided mint chutney, raita and salad with the order. Thumbs up for that. Definitely gonna try out more items from the menu in future.

2. Khade masale ka murg with butter roti - the khada masala was really delicious and spicy. It had full blown Masalas with a whole load of succulent chicken pieces.

featured_reviews.name: Rajat Bajaj
featured_reviews.review_text:
Our lunch at Punjab Grill, Phoenix Palladium Mall, turned out to be one of the most satisfying and comforting North Indian meals we’ve had in Mumbai. Being from North India, we always look for places that can recreate authentic flavours, and Punjab Grill once again lived up to expectations with its rich taste, warm ambience, and excellent service.

We ordered our all-time favourites — Dal Makhani and Paneer Lababdar, accompanied by Lachha Paranthas, Tandoori Rotis, and fresh salads. The Dal Makhani was slow-cooked to perfection, creamy, smoky, and just the right amount of buttery, reminding us of dhabas back home. The Paneer Lababdar was equally delicious: soft paneer cubes in a luscious, mildly spicy gravy that paired beautifully with the hot, crisp Lachha Paranthas. The Tandoori Rotis were perfectly roasted, light, and complemented the curries well. Every dish carried an unmistakable authentic North Indian aroma and taste.

The ambience of the restaurant added to the experience — elegant but cosy, with comfortable seating and warm lighting that made the meal feel unhurried and enjoyable. The environment was calm despite the mall rush, making it a great spot to relax after a movie.

What truly stood out was the courteous and attentive staff. They served promptly, checked in without being intrusive, and ensured every dish was fresh and hot. At the end of the meal, the liquid mouth freshener served in tiny tequila-style glasses was a delightful touch — refreshing, unique, and a fun way to conclude the lunch.

Overall, Punjab Grill offered a wonderful blend of flavour, comfort, and hospitality. For anyone craving authentic North Indian food in Mumbai, this place is always a dependable choice. A memorable lunch indeed!
